decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom was only being released in Q1/2019, so it is too early to judge it against aspirations, and the firm's dosimetry business gives it the slack to carry it through the ramp-up.

Small volume chambers are core consumables for small-field dosimetry in a stable, regulated market, so a newly launched model shows no performance shortfall that would trigger search for other uses of the resources.
Although it overlaps with Product B, chamber portfolios are routinely broad to fit different detector needs, and it costs little to keep a recent launch on the market.
The standard clinical chamber line with several models is a staple of absolute dosimetry and calibration that likely meets aspirations and supports the core business.
Relative dosimetry chambers pair with the firm's water phantoms and QA workflow, so they reinforce the established business rather than drain it.
Thimble chambers are long-lived standard products, and one year after launch there is no evidence of a shortfall that would justify dropping it.
